results.title: GPT-6.1 Terra vs Soul vs Luna: Which One Should You Use? | MindStudio
results.content:
GPT-6.1 Terra is the middle tier of OpenAI’s three-model GPT-6.1 family, sitting between the lightweight Luna and the flagship Soul. OpenAI positions Terra as a faster, cheaper alternative to Soul aimed at computer-use tasks, roughly half the cost of Soul with quicker response times. The catch is that it also gives up a meaningful chunk of reasoning quality compared to Soul, while still costing more than Luna. That middle-of-the-road positioning is the whole story with Terra: it’s not the cheap option and it’s not the smart option, it’s the option in between.

## TL;DR [...] GPT-6.1 Terra costs about half of what Soul costs and runs faster, but testers found it noticeably less capable on complex tasks like 3D generation and agentic reasoning.
 GPT-6.1 Luna is the budget pick, with input costs roughly ten times cheaper than Terra and output costs around ten times cheaper too, making it the better deal for simple, high-volume tasks.
 GPT-6.1 Soul remains the model worth paying for when a task needs real horsepower, since it produced dramatically better results than Terra in side-by-side 3D modeling tests.
 On Agent’s Last Exam, Terra reportedly beats GPT-5.6, but in hands-on use across real tasks it often performed closer to Luna than to Soul. [...] ## Which GPT-6.1 model should you actually use?

The practical breakdown looks like this: pick Luna for cheap, high-volume, low-complexity computer-use tasks where speed and cost matter more than polish. Pick Soul when the task requires real reasoning depth, creative judgment, or complex multi-step output, and you’re willing to pay more for it. Terra mostly makes sense if you specifically want something faster than Soul but smarter than Luna and don’t mind giving up quality on harder tasks to get there, though multiple comparisons suggest that gap is bigger than the pricing alone implies.
